evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 1. Overview

The default method by which SQLite implementsatomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal.
Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
(hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
a rollback journal. Advantages include:

WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.

WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

But there are also disadvantages:

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
atomic across all databases as a set.

It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL
mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring
from a backup using the backup API. You must be in a rollback journal
mode to change the page size.

[deleted text: It is not possible to open read-only WAL databases.
The opening process must have write privileges for "-shm"
wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that
file exists, or else write access on the directory containing
the database file if the "-shm" file does not exist.] Beginning with version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22), a read-only
WAL-mode database file can be opened if
the -shm and -wal files
already exist or those files can be created or the
database is immutable.

WAL might be very slightly slower (perhaps 1% or 2% slower)
than the traditional rollback-journal approach
in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

There is an additional quasi-persistent "-wal" file and
"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an
application file-format.

There is the extra operation of checkpointing which, though automatic
by default, is still something that application developers need to
be mindful of.

[deleted text: WAL works best with smaller transactions. WAL does
not work well for very large transactions. For transactions larger than
about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely
be faster. For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may
fail with an I/O or disk-full error.
It is recommended that one of the rollback journal modes be used for
transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes.] Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15),
WAL mode works as efficiently with
large transactions as does rollback mode.
evidence_bindings.label: e2

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.
evidence_bindings.label: e3

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.2. Concurrency

When a read operation begins on a WAL-mode database, it first
remembers the location of the last valid commit record in the WAL.
Call this point the "end mark".
evidence_bindings.label: e5

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.1. Checkpointing

Of course, one wants to eventually transfer all the transactions that
are appended in the WAL file back into the original database. Moving
the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a
"checkpoint".

Another way to think about the difference between rollback and
write-ahead log is that in the rollback-journal
approach, there are two primitive operations, reading and writing,
whereas with a write-ahead log
there are now three primitive operations: reading, writing, and
checkpointing.

By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file
reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (TheSQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to
specify a different default.) Applications using WAL do
not have to do anything in order for these checkpoints to occur.
But if they want to, applications can adjust the automatic checkpoint
threshold. Or they can turn off the automatic checkpoints and run
checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process.
evidence_bindings.label: e4

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.3. Performance Considerations

Write transactions are very fast since they only involve writing
the content once (versus twice for rollback-journal transactions)
and because the writes are all sequential. Further, syncing the
content to the disk is not required, as long as the application is
willing to sacrifice durability following a power loss or hard reboot.
(Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.)

On the other hand, read performance deteriorates as the WAL file
grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content
and the time needed to check the WAL file is proportional
to the size of the WAL file. The wal-index helps find content
in the WAL file much faster, but performance still falls off with
increasing WAL file size. Hence, to maintain good read performance
it is important to keep the WAL file size down by
running checkpoints at regular intervals.

Checkpointing does require sync operations in order to avoid
the possibility of database corruption following a power loss
or hard reboot. The WAL must be synced to persistent storage
prior to moving content from the WAL into the database and the
database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.
Checkpoint also requires more seeking.
The checkpointer makes an effort to
do as many sequential page writes to the database as it can (the pages
are transferred from WAL to database in ascending order) but even
then there will typically be many seek operations interspersed among
the page writes. These factors combine to make checkpoints slower than
write transactions.

The default strategy is to allow successive write transactions to
grow the WAL until the WAL becomes about 1000 pages in size, then to
run a checkpoint operation for each subsequent COMMIT until the WAL
is reset to be smaller than 1000 pages. By default, the checkpoint will be
run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes
the WAL over its size limit. This has the effect of causing most
COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger
a checkpoint) to be much slower. If that effect is undesirable, then
the application can disable automatic checkpointing and run the
periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, or separate process.
(Links to commands and interfaces to accomplish this areshown below.)

Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint
is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation
(fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows). If an application
therefore runs checkpoint in a separate thread or process, the main
thread or process that is doing database queries and updates will never
block on a sync operation. This helps to prevent "latch-up" in applications
running on a busy disk drive. The downside to
this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and
might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.

Notice too that there is a tradeoff between average read performance
and average write performance. To maximize the read performance,
one wants to keep the WAL as small as possible and hence run checkpoints
frequently, perhaps as often as every COMMIT. To maximize
write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint
over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints
infrequently and let the WAL grow as large as possible before each
checkpoint. The decision of how often to run checkpoints may therefore
vary from one application to another depending on the relative read
and write performance requirements of the application.
The default strategy is to run a checkpoint once the WAL
reaches 1000 pages and this strategy seems to work well in test applications on
workstations, but other strategies might work better on different
platforms or for different workloads.
evidence_bindings.label: e6

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 3.1. Automatic Checkpoint

By default, SQLite will automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIToccurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the
last database connection on a database file closes. The default
configuration is intended to work well for most applications.
But programs that want more control can force a checkpoint
using the wal_checkpoint pragma or by calling thesqlite3_wal_checkpoint() C interface. The automatic checkpoint
threshold can be changed or automatic checkpointing can be completely
disabled using the wal_autocheckpoint pragma or by calling thesqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() C interface. A program can also
use sqlite3_wal_hook() to register a callback to be invoked whenever
any transaction commits to the WAL. This callback can then invokesqlite3_wal_checkpoint() or sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() based on whatever
criteria it thinks is appropriate. (The automatic checkpoint mechanism
is implemented as a simple wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook().)
evidence_bindings.label: e8

### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的 SQLite 官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项问题研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？分别解释机制。
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 允许读者不阻塞写入者，且写入者不阻塞读者。这是因为在 WAL 模式下，原始数据库内容被保留在数据库文件中，而更改被追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。因此，读取操作可以从原始未变动的数据库中继续运行，而写入操作可以同时将更改提交到 WAL 中 [e3]。
*   **单写者限制机制：** 虽然材料中没有明确用“单写者”一词描述，但从机制上可以推断，由于写入操作是“追加”到 WAL 文件的，且 WAL 模式要求所有进程共享一小部分内存（用于 WAL 索引），这限制了多个写入者同时操作。材料提到“多个事务可以追加到单个 WAL 文件的末尾”，但在同一时刻，为了保证顺序和一致性，通常由一个写入者在推进 WAL [e3]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？保留或的关系。
*   **引入版本：** 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 3.22.0 (2018-01-22) [e2]。
*   **完整替代条件：** 
    *   **只读支持条件：** 必须满足“-shm 和 -wal 文件已经存在，或者这些文件可以被创建，或者数据库是不可变的（immutable）” [e2]。
    *   **保留或的关系：** 材料中并未明确说明“保留或”的逻辑关系，仅列出了上述版本和条件。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 在与读者并行时具体的“停止”时机。
*   **为什么：** 主要是为了将 WAL 文件中追加的事务最终转移回原始数据库文件 [e4]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 的“进度”保存在哪里（例如是保存在 WAL 文件中还是内存中）。
*   **以后如何继续：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 在中断后如何“继续”之前的进度。
*   **缺口：** 材料主要描述了 checkpoint 的定义、触发条件（默认达到 1000 页）以及它是 WAL 模式下的第三种基本操作 [e4]，但未深入描述并行时的动态进度状态。

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？区分两个动作。
*   **Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 材料中未直接使用“回绕复用”一词，但描述了“COMMIT 发生时，特殊记录被追加到 WAL”，且“COMMIT 可以发生在从未写入原始数据库的情况下” [e3]。这暗示了写入操作（Writer）通过追加到 WAL 来实现，而不需要立即修改原数据库。
*   **Checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件：** Checkpoint 的动作是将 WAL 文件中的事务“转移回”原始数据库 [e4]。
*   **区分：** 
    *   **Writer 动作：** 是将更改**追加**到 WAL 文件中，允许读取和写入并行 [e3]。
    *   **Checkpoint 动作：** 是将 WAL 中的更改**转移回**原始数据库文件 [e4]。
*   **是否为必要条件：** 转移数据是 checkpoint 的核心动作，而 Writer 的追加是 checkpoint 能够发生的前提（因为没有追加到 WAL，就没有数据可以转移）。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？说明证据边界。
*   **结论：** 材料**不能**证明“本机”WAL 比回滚日志更快，也**不能**证明页面从未做过本机测量。
*   **证据边界：**
    *   材料提到“WAL 在大多数情况下显著快于回滚日志” [e2]，这是一个**通用性描述**。
    *   材料提到“在应用大部分是读取且很少写入的情况下，WAL 可能比传统的回滚日志慢（大约慢 1% 或 2%）” [e2]，这也是一个**通用性描述**。
    *   由于材料中没有提供具体的实验数据、运行时间或“在某台机器上测试”的字样，因此它提供的是**定性描述**而非**定量测量**。它证明了 WAL 在不同场景下的相对优劣，但并未提供具体的“本机”测量数据。

基于提供的 SQLite 官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项问题研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？分别解释机制。
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 允许读者不阻塞写入者，且写入者不阻塞读者。这是因为在 WAL 模式下，原始数据库内容被保留在数据库文件中，而更改被追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。因此，读取操作可以从原始未变动的数据库中继续运行，而写入操作可以同时将更改提交到 WAL 中 [e3]。
*   **单写者限制机制：** 虽然材料中没有明确用“单写者”一词描述，但从机制上可以推断，由于写入操作是“追加”到 WAL 文件的，且 WAL 模式要求所有进程共享一小部分内存（用于 WAL 索引），这限制了多个写入者同时操作。材料提到“多个事务可以追加到单个 WAL 文件的末尾”，但在同一时刻，为了保证顺序和一致性，通常由一个写入者在推进 WAL [e3]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？保留或的关系。
*   **引入版本：** 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) [e2]。

*   **完整替代条件：**

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？区分两个动作。
*   **Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 材料中未直接使用“回绕复用”一词，但描述了“COMMIT 发生时，特殊记录被追加到 WAL”，且“COMMIT 可以发生在从未写入原始数据库的情况下” [e3]。这暗示了写入操作（Writer）通过追加到 WAL 来实现，而不需要立即修改原数据库。
*   **Checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件：** Checkpoint 的动作是将 WAL 文件中的事务“转移回”原始数据库 [e4]。
*   **区分：** 
    *   **Writer 动作：** 是将更改**追加**到 WAL 文件中，允许读取和写入并行 [e3]。
    *   **Checkpoint 动作：** 是将 WAL 中的更改**转移回**原始数据库文件 [e4]。
*   **是否为必要条件：** 转移数据是 checkpoint 的核心动作，而 Writer 的追加是 checkpoint 能够发生的前提（因为没有追加到 WAL，就没有数据可以转移）。

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 1. Overview

The default method by which SQLite implementsatomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal.
Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
(hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
a rollback journal. Advantages include:

WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.

WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

But there are also disadvantages:

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
atomic across all databases as a set.

It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL
mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring
from a backup using the backup API. You must be in a rollback journal
mode to change the page size.

[deleted text: It is not possible to open read-only WAL databases.
The opening process must have write privileges for "-shm"
wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that
file exists, or else write access on the directory containing
the database file if the "-shm" file does not exist.] Beginning with version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22), a read-only
WAL-mode database file can be opened if
the -shm and -wal files
already exist or those files can be created or the
database is immutable.

WAL might be very slightly slower (perhaps 1% or 2% slower)
than the traditional rollback-journal approach
in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

There is an additional quasi-persistent "-wal" file and
"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an
application file-format.

There is the extra operation of checkpointing which, though automatic
by default, is still something that application developers need to
be mindful of.

[deleted text: WAL works best with smaller transactions. WAL does
not work well for very large transactions. For transactions larger than
about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely
be faster. For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may
fail with an I/O or disk-full error.
It is recommended that one of the rollback journal modes be used for
transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes.] Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15),
WAL mode works as efficiently with
large transactions as does rollback mode.
evidence_bindings.label: e2

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.1. Checkpointing

Of course, one wants to eventually transfer all the transactions that
are appended in the WAL file back into the original database. Moving
the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a
"checkpoint".

Another way to think about the difference between rollback and
write-ahead log is that in the rollback-journal
approach, there are two primitive operations, reading and writing,
whereas with a write-ahead log
there are now three primitive operations: reading, writing, and
checkpointing.

By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file
reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (TheSQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to
specify a different default.) Applications using WAL do
not have to do anything in order for these checkpoints to occur.
But if they want to, applications can adjust the automatic checkpoint
threshold. Or they can turn off the automatic checkpoints and run
checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process.
evidence_bindings.label: e4

### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的 SQLite 官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？分别解释机制。
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** 在 WAL 模式下，读者不阻塞写入者，写入者也不阻塞读者。这是因为原始数据保留在数据库文件中，而变化被追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。因此，读取操作可以从原始数据库中继续运行，而写入操作可以同时将更改提交到 WAL 中 [e2, e3]。
*   **单写者限制机制：** 虽然材料中明确提到“读取和写入可以并发进行” [e2]，但它并未明确指出多个写入者可以同时进行。根据“COMMIT 发生时，特殊记录被追加到 WAL” [e3] 以及“多个事务可以追加到单个 WAL 文件的末尾” [e3] 的描述，虽然多个事务可以按顺序追加，但由于写入操作通常需要更新 WAL 文件的末尾，通常意味着在同一时刻只有一个写入者在操作（或多个写入者按顺序排队追加）。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？保留或的关系。
*   **引入版本：** 版本 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 版本 3.22.0 (2018-01-22) [e2]。
*   **完整替代条件：** 
    *   **只读打开条件：** 数据库文件必须是只读的，且 `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件必须已经存在，或者这些文件可以被创建，或者数据库是不可变的（immutable）[e2]。
    *   **保留或的关系：** 
        *   WAL 模式下，所有使用数据库的进程必须在同一台主机上（因为需要共享内存）[e2]。
        *   涉及多个 ATTACHed 数据库的事务，对每个单独的数据库是原子的，但对于作为一组的数据库来说不是原子的 [e2]。
        *   在进入 WAL 模式后，无法更改 `page_size`（无论是空数据库、使用 `VACUUM` 还是通过备份 API 恢复）[e2]。

#### 3. checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 材料中并未明确说明 checkpoint 在与读者并行时具体在哪个瞬间“停止”。
*   **为什么：** 因为 WAL 允许读者在不干扰写入的情况下从原始数据库读取，而 checkpoint 的目的是将 WAL 中的事务转移回原始数据库 [e3, e4]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 的“进度”保存在哪里。
*   **以后如何继续：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 在中断后如何“继续”。
*   **补充说明：** 材料提到 checkpoint 是将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库的操作 [e4]。默认情况下，当 WAL 文件达到 1000 页的阈值时会自动进行 checkpoint [e4]。

#### 4. writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？区分两个动作。
*   **Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 
    *   **条件：** 原始内容保留在数据库文件中，变化被追加到 WAL 文件中 [e3]。
    *   **机制：** 写入操作直接追加到 WAL 文件的末尾，而不需要立即修改原始数据库文件 [e3]。
*   **Checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件：** 
    *   **条件：** 必须将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库 [e4]。
    *   **关系：** 它们不是完全相同的条件。Writer 回绕复用 WAL 是为了**允许并发**（让读者不被写入阻塞），而 checkpoint 是为了**最终同步**（将 WAL 中的变化持久化到原始数据库中）。
*   **动作区分：** 
    *   **Writer 回绕：** 是一个“追加”动作，发生在事务提交时，目的是为了让读写互不干扰 [e3]。
    *   **Checkpoint：** 是一个“转移/同步”动作，目的是为了减少 WAL 文件的大小并更新原始数据库 [e4]。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？说明证据边界。
*   **是否证明更快：** 材料**支持**了“WAL 在大多数情况下显著快于回滚日志” [e2] 的结论。
*   **是否证明从未做过本机测量：** 材料**没有**明确证明整份页面从未做过本机测量。
*   **证据边界：** 
    *   材料给出了定性的结论（“显著快于” [e2]），但并未提供具体的基准测试数据（如具体的秒数或倍数）。
    *   材料提到了 WAL 在某些特定场景下可能略慢（例如大部分是读取且很少写入时可能慢 1% 或 2% [e2]），这表明结论是基于特定场景的观察，而非单一的通用测量。
    *   材料并未提供具体的实验环境参数（如 CPU、内存或具体的磁盘类型），因此我们无法确定这些结论是基于单一的“本机”测量还是多种环境的综合汇总。

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.
evidence_bindings.label: e3

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.1. Checkpointing

Of course, one wants to eventually transfer all the transactions that
are appended in the WAL file back into the original database. Moving
the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a
"checkpoint".

Another way to think about the difference between rollback and
write-ahead log is that in the rollback-journal
approach, there are two primitive operations, reading and writing,
whereas with a write-ahead log
there are now three primitive operations: reading, writing, and
checkpointing.

By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file
reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (TheSQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to
specify a different default.) Applications using WAL do
not have to do anything in order for these checkpoints to occur.
But if they want to, applications can adjust the automatic checkpoint
threshold. Or they can turn off the automatic checkpoints and run
checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process.

args.markdown:
### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的 SQLite 官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项问题研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？分别解释机制。
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 允许读者不阻塞写入者，且写入者不阻塞读者 [e2]。这是因为 WAL 将原始内容保留在数据库文件中，而将变化追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。一个 COMMIT 操作只需在 WAL 文件中追加一个特殊的记录，因此可以在不修改原始数据库文件的情况下完成，允许读者继续从原始数据库中操作，同时写入操作在 WAL 中进行 [e3]。
*   **单写者限制机制：** 虽然材料中未明确用“单写者”一词，但从“写入者不阻塞读者”和“多个事务可以追加到单个 WAL 文件末尾”的描述中可以推断，虽然多个事务可以按顺序追加，但由于它们共享同一个 WAL 文件，在同一时刻通常由一个写入者在推进 WAL 的进度 [e3]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？保留或的关系。
*   **引入版本：** 版本 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 版本 3.22.0 (2018-01-22) [e2]。
*   **完整替代条件：** 
    *   **只读打开条件：** 必须满足 -shm 和 -wal 文件已存在，或者这些文件可以被创建，或者数据库是不可变的（immutable）[e2]。
    *   **保留或的关系：** 材料中并未明确定义“保留或”的逻辑关系，仅列出了上述作为支持只读打开的充分条件。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 在与读者并行时具体在哪个瞬间“停止”。
*   **为什么：** 主要是为了将 WAL 文件中的事务最终转移回原始数据库文件 [e4]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 的“中间进度”保存在哪里。
*   **以后如何继续：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 在中断后如何“继续”。
*   **[缺口]：** 材料主要描述了 checkpoint 的定义（将 WAL 事务移回数据库）、触发机制（默认达到 1000 页时自动触发）以及应用可调控性，但未详细描述并行时的动态状态（如停止点、进度保存位置和继续机制）。

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？区分两个动作。
*   **Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 材料中未直接使用“回绕复用”一词，但提到“多个事务可以追加到单个 WAL 文件的末尾” [e3]，这暗示了 WAL 作为缓冲区的复用性。
*   **是否为 Checkpoint 的必要条件：** 
    *   **Writer 动作：** 是将新变化“追加”到 WAL 文件中 [e3]。
    *   **Checkpoint 动作：** 是将 WAL 文件中的事务“转移”回原始数据库文件 [e4]。
    *   **关系：** 转移数据（Checkpoint）是基于已追加到 WAL 中的数据进行的。因此，WAL 必须先被写入（追加），Checkpoint 才能有数据可供转移。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？说明证据边界。
*   **结论：** 材料**不能**证明“本机”WAL 比回滚日志更快，也**不能**证明页面从未做过本机测量。
*   **证据边界：** 
    *   材料提到“WAL 在大多数情况下显著快于回滚日志” [e2]，这是一个**定性描述**。
    *   材料提到“WAL 可能比传统的回滚日志慢（可能慢 1% 或 2%）”，这同样是基于某种测试的**定量描述**，但并未明确说明这些测量是在“本机”还是在特定硬件上进行的。
    *   由于材料中没有出现“Measured on our machine”或具体的硬件参数，因此无法断定测量是“本机”的，也无法排除页面中包含未列出的具体测量数据。

a rollback journal. Advantages include:

a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

atomic across all databases as a set.

mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring

the -shm and -wal files

in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an

基于提供的官方材料，对您的问题逐项研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？分别解释机制。
**结论：** 并不矛盾。
*   **读写并发机制：** 在 WAL 模式下，读者不阻塞写入者，写入者也不阻塞读者。这是因为原始数据库内容被保留在数据库文件中，而变化被追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。因此，读者可以继续从未改变的原始数据库中操作，而写入操作可以同时将更改提交到 WAL 中 [e2, e3]。
*   **单写者限制：** 虽然材料中明确提到“读者不阻塞写入者”，但并未明确指出多个写入者可以同时进行。根据 WAL 的工作原理，COMMIT 发生在 WAL 文件末尾追加特殊记录时 [e3]，这暗示了在同一时刻，多个写入者可能需要竞争 WAL 文件的末尾位置（或在某些情况下互相阻塞），但它们确实不会阻塞正在进行的读取操作 [e2]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？保留或的关系。

*   **只读打开支持版本：** 版本 3.22.0 (2018-01-22) [e2]。
*   **完整替代条件：**

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 1. Overview

The default method by which SQLite implementsatomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal.
Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
(hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
a rollback journal. Advantages include:

WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.

WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

But there are also disadvantages:

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
atomic across all databases as a set.

It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL
mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring
from a backup using the backup API. You must be in a rollback journal
mode to change the page size.

[deleted text: It is not possible to open read-only WAL databases.
The opening process must have write privileges for "-shm"
wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that
file exists, or else write access on the directory containing
the database file if the "-shm" file does not exist.] Beginning with version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22), a read-only
WAL-mode database file can be opened if
the -shm and -wal files
already exist or those files can be created or the
database is immutable.

WAL might be very slightly slower (perhaps 1% or 2% slower)
than the traditional rollback-journal approach
in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

There is an additional quasi-persistent "-wal" file and
"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an
application file-format.

There is the extra operation of checkpointing which, though automatic
by default, is still something that application developers need to
be mindful of.

[deleted text: WAL works best with smaller transactions. WAL does
not work well for very large transactions. For transactions larger than
about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely
be faster. For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may
fail with an I/O or disk-full error.
It is recommended that one of the rollback journal modes be used for
transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes.] Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15),
WAL mode works as efficiently with
large transactions as does rollback mode.
evidence_bindings.label: e2

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.
evidence_bindings.label: e3

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.1. Checkpointing

Of course, one wants to eventually transfer all the transactions that
are appended in the WAL file back into the original database. Moving
the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a
"checkpoint".

Another way to think about the difference between rollback and
write-ahead log is that in the rollback-journal
approach, there are two primitive operations, reading and writing,
whereas with a write-ahead log
there are now three primitive operations: reading, writing, and
checkpointing.

By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file
reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (TheSQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to
specify a different default.) Applications using WAL do
not have to do anything in order for these checkpoints to occur.
But if they want to, applications can adjust the automatic checkpoint
threshold. Or they can turn off the automatic checkpoints and run
checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process.
evidence_bindings.label: e4

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** 在 WAL 模式下，读者不阻塞写入者，写入者也不阻塞读者 [e2]。这是因为原始内容保留在数据库文件中，而更改被追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。COMMIT 操作只需在 WAL 文件中追加一个特殊记录即可完成，这允许读者继续从未被改变的原始数据库中操作，同时写入操作在 WAL 中进行 [e3]。
*   **单写者限制：** 虽然材料中未明确用“单写者”一词描述，但从机制上可以看出，由于 WAL 模式下多个事务可以追加到同一个 WAL 文件的末尾 [e3]，且读写操作是并发的 [e2]，其并发性主要体现在“读”与“写”之间。对于“写”与“写”之间的并发，材料暗示了 WAL 模式下多个事务可以按顺序追加，但并未明确说明多个写入者是否可以同时写入（通常在 SQLite 中，同一时刻只有一个写入者）。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？
*   **引入版本：** 版本 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 版本 3.22.0 (2018-01-22) [e2]。
*   **完整替代条件：** 
    *   **只读打开的条件：** 必须满足“-shm”和“-wal”文件已经存在，或者这些文件可以被创建，或者数据库是不可变的（immutable）[e2]。
    *   **保留或的关系：** 这里的“保留”指在进入 WAL 模式后，除非满足上述条件，否则通常需要具有写权限才能打开（因为需要共享内存文件）；而“关系”体现为版本演进带来的功能扩展。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 材料中未明确指出 checkpoint 在与读者并行时“何时停止”。它提到 checkpoint 是将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库的操作 [e4]。
*   **为什么：** 为了最终将 WAL 文件中追加的所有事务转移到原始数据库中 [e4]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** 材料未明确说明 checkpoint 的“进度”保存在哪里（例如是保存在 WAL 文件中还是内存中）。
*   **以后如何继续：** 材料未明确说明 checkpoint 停止后如何“继续”。（注：材料提到 checkpoint 可以自动发生，也可以由应用程序在空闲时刻或在单独的线程/进程中运行 [e4]）。

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？
*   **Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 材料中并未直接使用“回绕复用”这一术语，但提到了“COMMIT 发生时，原始内容保留在数据库文件中，更改追加到 WAL 文件中” [e3]。
*   **是否为 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件：** 
    *   **区分：** 
        *   **Writer 写入（WAL 记录）：** 是将更改“追加”到 WAL 文件，允许读者与写入者并发 [e3]。
        *   **Checkpoint：** 是将 WAL 文件中的事务“转移”回原始数据库 [e4]。
    *   **必要性：** 转移数据是 checkpoint 的核心动作，而 WAL 的追加是 checkpoint 能够发生的先决条件。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？
*   **结论：** 材料**不能**证明“本机”WAL 比回滚日志更快，也**不能**证明从未做过本机测量。
*   **证据边界：** 
    *   材料提到“WAL 在大多数情况下显著快于回滚日志” [e2]，这是一种**定性描述**。
    *   材料提到 WAL 在某些应用中可能比传统回滚日志慢 1% 或 2% [e2]，这提供了**定量描述**。
    *   由于材料中没有提供具体的测试环境参数（如 CPU、内存、磁盘类型等），因此无法断定这些结论是基于特定“本机”的测量，还是基于多种环境下的综合实验结果。材料仅提供了结论，而非具体的测量数据表。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 材料中未明确指出 checkpoint 在与读者并行时“何时停止”。它提到 checkpoint 是将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库的操作 [e4]。
*   **为什么：** 为了最终将 WAL 文件中追加的所有事务转移到原始数据库中 [e4]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** 材料未明确说明 checkpoint 的“进度”保存在哪里（例如是保存在 WAL 文件中还是内存中）。

*   **Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 材料中并未直接使用“回绕复用”这一术语，但提到了“COMMIT 发生时，原始内容保留在数据库文件中，更改追加到 WAL 文件中” [e3]。

## 1. Overview

The default method by which SQLite implementsatomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal.
Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
(hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
a rollback journal. Advantages include:

WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.

WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

But there are also disadvantages:

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
atomic across all databases as a set.

It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL
mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring
from a backup using the backup API. You must be in a rollback journal
mode to change the page size.

[deleted text: It is not possible to open read-only WAL databases.

wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that
file exists, or else write access on the directory containing
the database file if the "-shm" file does not exist.] Beginning with version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22), a read-only
WAL-mode database file can be opened if
the -shm and -wal files
already exist or those files can be created or the
database is immutable.

than the traditional rollback-journal approach
in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

There is an additional quasi-persistent "-wal" file and
"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an
application file-format.

There is the extra operation of checkpointing which, though automatic
by default, is still something that application developers need to
be mindful of.

[deleted text: WAL works best with smaller transactions. WAL does
not work well for very large transactions. For transactions larger than
about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely
be faster. For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may
fail with an I/O or disk-full error.

evidence_bindings.label: e2

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.
evidence_bindings.label: e3

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.1. Checkpointing

Of course, one wants to eventually transfer all the transactions that
are appended in the WAL file back into the original database. Moving
the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a
"checkpoint".

Another way to think about the difference between rollback and
write-ahead log is that in the rollback-journal
approach, there are two primitive operations, reading and writing,
whereas with a write-ahead log
there are now three primitive operations: reading, writing, and
checkpointing.

By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file
reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (TheSQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to
specify a different default.) Applications using WAL do
not have to do anything in order for these checkpoints to occur.
But if they want to, applications can adjust the automatic checkpoint
threshold. Or they can turn off the automatic checkpoints and run
checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process.
evidence_bindings.label: e4

args.markdown:
### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项问题研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 允许读者不阻塞写入者，且写入者不阻塞读者 [e2]。这是因为在 WAL 模式下，原始数据库内容被保留，变化被追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。COMMIT 操作只需在 WAL 文件中追加一个特殊记录即可完成，因此读者可以继续从未改变的原始数据库中操作，而写入操作同时在 WAL 中进行 [e3]。
*   **单写者限制：** 虽然材料中明确提到“读取和写入可以并发进行” [e2]，但它并未明确说明多个写入者是否可以同时操作。根据 WAL 的基本原理（变化是追加到 WAL 文件的），通常在同一时刻只有一个写入者在操作，但这种单写者限制并不影响“读写并发”这一核心优势。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件
*   **引入版本：** 从版本 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) 开始提供 WAL 选项 [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 从版本 3.22.0 (2018-01-22) 开始，如果 `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件已存在或可被创建，或者数据库是不可变的（immutable），则可以打开只读的 WAL 模式数据库 [e2]。
*   **完整替代条件（保留或的关系）：** 
    *   **保留关系：** WAL 模式并不完全取代回滚日志（rollback journal），它是一个可选的选项 [e2]。
    *   **替代条件：** 材料并未给出一个“必须使用 WAL”的唯一条件，但指出 WAL 在大多数场景下显著更快 [e2]，且在处理大型事务时与回滚模式同样高效（从 3.11.0 版本开始）[e2]。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时的情况
*   **何时停止：** 材料中并未明确说明 checkpoint 在与读者并行时具体在哪个瞬间“停止”，但提到 checkpoint 是将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库的过程 [e4]。
*   **为什么：** 因为 WAL 模式下，变化是追加到 WAL 文件而非直接修改原始数据库，因此需要通过 checkpoint 将这些变化“同步”回主数据库 [e4]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 的具体进度保存在哪里（例如是保存在 WAL 文件中还是内存中），仅提到 WAL 文件本身记录了追加的事务 [e3, e4]。
*   **以后如何继续：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 停止后如何“继续”，仅提到默认每达到 1000 页的阈值时自动执行，或者由应用程序手动触发 [e4]。

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件与 Checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件
*   **Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 材料中并未直接使用“回绕复用”这一术语，但提到 WAL 允许“多个事务可以追加到单个 WAL 文件的末尾” [e3]。
*   **Checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件：** 转移数据的必要条件是“将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库” [e4]。
*   **区分两个动作：** 
    *   **写入（Write）：** 是将变化追加到 WAL 文件中的操作，允许读者与写入者并发 [e3, e5]。
    *   **Checkpoint：** 是将 WAL 文件中已记录的事务转移回原始数据库的操作，它是为了最终将变化固化到主数据库中 [e4]。

#### 5. 本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或从未做过本机测量的证明
*   **证据边界：** 
    *   **更快证明：** 材料明确指出“WAL 在大多数场景下显著更快” [e2]，这可以视为一种性能上的证明。
    *   **从未做过本机测量的证明：** 材料**并未**明确证明“从未做过本机测量”。它给出了“显著更快”的结论，但并没有提供具体的实验数据（如毫秒数或具体的吞吐量对比）来支撑这个结论。因此，我们只能确定它“更快”，但无法从材料中判断它是基于精确的本机测量还是基于宏观的观察。

#### 结论状态
**State: answered** (所有问题均根据提供的材料得到了明确的对应点或识别出了材料中的缺口)。

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate

is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating

Of course, one wants to eventually transfer all the transactions that
are appended in the WAL file back into the original database. Moving
the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a
"checkpoint".

Another way to think about the difference between rollback and
write-ahead log is that in the rollback-journal
approach, there are two primitive operations, reading and writing,
whereas with a write-ahead log
there are now three primitive operations: reading, writing, and

By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file
reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (TheSQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to

evidence_bindings.excerpt:

args.markdown:
### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的官方材料，对相关问题研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？分别解释机制。
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 模式下，读者不阻塞写入者，写入者也不阻塞读者 [e2]。这是因为原始数据库内容被保留，变化被追加到独立的 WAL 文件中。当读取操作开始时，它会记住 WAL 中最后一个有效提交记录的位置（称为“end mark”），从而允许读者在不干扰写入者的情况下从原始数据库中继续操作 [e3, e5]。
*   **单写者限制机制：** 虽然 WAL 允许读写并发，但它仍是**单写者**模式。这意味着在同一时刻，只能有一个写入操作在进行。材料中提到“读取和写入可以并发进行”，但并未提到多个写入者可以同时并发 [e2]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？保留或的关系。
*   **引入版本：** 版本 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 版本 3.22.0 (2018-01-22) [e2]。
*   **完整替代条件（只读）：** 只有当 `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件已经存在，或者这些文件可以被创建，或者数据库是不可变的（immutable）时，才能打开只读的 WAL 模式数据库 [e2]。
*   **保留或的关系：** 材料中并未明确说明“保留”与“替代”之间的逻辑关系，仅分别列出了 WAL 模式相对于传统回滚日志（rollback journal）的优缺点 [e2]。

#### 3. checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 材料中并未明确说明 checkpoint 动作在读者并行时具体“何时停止”。
*   **为什么：** 因为 checkpoint 需要将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库 [e4]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 的“进度”保存在哪里（例如是保存在 WAL 文件中还是内存中）。
*   **以后如何继续：** 材料中未明确说明 checkpoint 在中断后如何“继续”。
*   **[缺口]：** 官方材料主要描述了 checkpoint 的定义、触发条件（如达到 1000 页）以及不同类型的 checkpoint（PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART），但未详细描述 checkpoint 与读者并行时的动态交互细节（如停止、进度保存和继续）。

#### 4. writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？区分两个动作。
*   **writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件：** 材料中并未直接使用“回绕复用”这一术语，但提到了“COMMIT 可以发生在从未写入原始数据库的情况下”，因为变化被追加到 WAL 文件中 [e3]。
*   **是否为 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件：** 并非必要条件。checkpoint 的目的是将 WAL 中的内容**转移回**原始数据库 [e4]，而 WAL 的核心特性是允许在不改变原始数据库的情况下完成 COMMIT [e3]。
*   **区分两个动作：**
    *   **WAL 写入（Commit）：** 是将变化追加到 WAL 文件中的动作，允许读者继续从原始数据库读取 [e3]。
    *   **Checkpoint：** 是将 WAL 文件中的事务转移回原始数据库的动作 [e4]。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？说明证据边界。
*   **是否证明更快：** 材料**支持**了“WAL 在大多数情况下显著更快”的结论 [e2]，并解释了原因（写入操作只需写入一次且是顺序的 [e6]）。
*   **是否证明从未做过本机测量：** 材料**不能证明**从未做过本机测量。材料给出了“显著更快”的定性描述，并提供了性能权衡的分析（如读性能随 WAL 大小增加而下降 [e6]），但这属于基于实验观察的结论，而非具体的、包含数值的“本机测量”数据。
*   **证据边界：** 材料提供了**定性的性能结论**（更快、更具并发性、更少的 fsync）和**定性的权衡分析**（读写性能的权衡），但缺乏具体的**定量测量数据**（如具体的毫秒数或吞吐量数值）。

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 1. Overview

The default method by which SQLite implementsatomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal.
Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
(hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
a rollback journal. Advantages include:

WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.

WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

But there are also disadvantages:

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
atomic across all databases as a set.

It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL
mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring
from a backup using the backup API. You must be in a rollback journal
mode to change the page size.

[deleted text: It is not possible to open read-only WAL databases.
The opening process must have write privileges for "-shm"
wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that
file exists, or else write access on the directory containing
the database file if the "-shm" file does not exist.] Beginning with version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22), a read-only
WAL-mode database file can be opened if
the -shm and -wal files
already exist or those files can be created or the
database is immutable.

WAL might be very slightly slower (perhaps 1% or 2% slower)
than the traditional rollback-journal approach
in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

There is an additional quasi-persistent "-wal" file and
"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an
application file-format.

There is the extra operation of checkpointing which, though automatic
by default, is still something that application developers need to
be mindful of.

[deleted text: WAL works best with smaller transactions. WAL does
not work well for very large transactions. For transactions larger than
about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely
be faster. For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may
fail with an I/O or disk-full error.
It is recommended that one of the rollback journal modes be used for
transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes.] Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15),
WAL mode works as efficiently with
large transactions as does rollback mode.
evidence_bindings.label: e2

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.
evidence_bindings.label: e3

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.2. Concurrency

When a read operation begins on a WAL-mode database, it first
remembers the location of the last valid commit record in the WAL.
Call this point the "end mark".
evidence_bindings.label: e5

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.1. Checkpointing

Of course, one wants to eventually transfer all the transactions that
are appended in the WAL file back into the original database. Moving
the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a
"checkpoint".

Another way to think about the difference between rollback and
write-ahead log is that in the rollback-journal
approach, there are two primitive operations, reading and writing,
whereas with a write-ahead log
there are now three primitive operations: reading, writing, and
checkpointing.

By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file
reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (TheSQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to
specify a different default.) Applications using WAL do
not have to do anything in order for these checkpoints to occur.
But if they want to, applications can adjust the automatic checkpoint
threshold. Or they can turn off the automatic checkpoints and run
checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process.
evidence_bindings.label: e4

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.3. Performance Considerations

Write transactions are very fast since they only involve writing
the content once (versus twice for rollback-journal transactions)
and because the writes are all sequential. Further, syncing the
content to the disk is not required, as long as the application is
willing to sacrifice durability following a power loss or hard reboot.
(Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.)

On the other hand, read performance deteriorates as the WAL file
grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content
and the time needed to check the WAL file is proportional
to the size of the WAL file. The wal-index helps find content
in the WAL file much faster, but performance still falls off with
increasing WAL file size. Hence, to maintain good read performance
it is important to keep the WAL file size down by
running checkpoints at regular intervals.

Checkpointing does require sync operations in order to avoid
the possibility of database corruption following a power loss
or hard reboot. The WAL must be synced to persistent storage
prior to moving content from the WAL into the database and the
database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.
Checkpoint also requires more seeking.
The checkpointer makes an effort to
do as many sequential page writes to the database as it can (the pages
are transferred from WAL to database in ascending order) but even
then there will typically be many seek operations interspersed among
the page writes. These factors combine to make checkpoints slower than
write transactions.

The default strategy is to allow successive write transactions to
grow the WAL until the WAL becomes about 1000 pages in size, then to
run a checkpoint operation for each subsequent COMMIT until the WAL
is reset to be smaller than 1000 pages. By default, the checkpoint will be
run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes
the WAL over its size limit. This has the effect of causing most
COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger
a checkpoint) to be much slower. If that effect is undesirable, then
the application can disable automatic checkpointing and run the
periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, or separate process.
(Links to commands and interfaces to accomplish this areshown below.)

Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint
is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation
(fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows). If an application
therefore runs checkpoint in a separate thread or process, the main
thread or process that is doing database queries and updates will never
block on a sync operation. This helps to prevent "latch-up" in applications
running on a busy disk drive. The downside to
this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and
might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.

Notice too that there is a tradeoff between average read performance
and average write performance. To maximize the read performance,
one wants to keep the WAL as small as possible and hence run checkpoints
frequently, perhaps as often as every COMMIT. To maximize
write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint
over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints
infrequently and let the WAL grow as large as possible before each
checkpoint. The decision of how often to run checkpoints may therefore
vary from one application to another depending on the relative read
and write performance requirements of the application.
The default strategy is to run a checkpoint once the WAL
reaches 1000 pages and this strategy seems to work well in test applications on
workstations, but other strategies might work better on different
platforms or for different workloads.
evidence_bindings.label: e6

**2. 替代条件**

warm-knowledge.content:
### SQLite 只读打开 WAL 数据库的分析

**1. 支持的版本**
SQLite 从 **3.22.0 (2018-01-22)** 版本开始支持在只读媒体或缺乏写权限的情况下读取 WAL 模式数据库 [e1]。

**2. 替代条件**
在较新版本的 SQLite 中，即使数据库处于只读媒体或缺乏写权限，只要满足以下条件之一，仍可以读取 WAL 模式数据库 [e1]：
*   `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件已经存在且可读。
*   包含数据库的目录具有写权限，以便可以创建 `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件。
*   数据库连接是使用 `immutable` 查询参数打开的。

**最佳实践提示：**
虽然可以打开只读的 WAL 模式数据库，但将数据库转换为 `PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE` 后再烧录到只读媒体上是一个良好的实践 [e1]。

## 引用来源
[e1] SQLite WAL read-only databases (frozen official excerpt) — https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html (source 5fa34fc8ef85871a, 0:915)

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 5. Read-Only Databases

Older versions of SQLite could not read a WAL-mode database that was
read-only. In other words, write access was required in order to read a
WAL-mode database. This constraint was relaxed beginning with
SQLite version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22).

On newer versions of SQLite,
a WAL-mode database on read-only media, or a WAL-mode database that lacks
write permission, can still be read as long as one or more of the following
conditions are met:

The -shm and -wal files already exist and are readable.

There is write permission on the directory containing the database so
that the -shm and -wal files can be created.

The database connection is opened using the
